description: Verify recovery from old duplicate SYN: DUT in LISTEN replies SYN,ACK to a stale SYN, consumes a tester-injected RST with believable seq, returns to LISTEN, and replies SYN,ACK to a fresh SYN (RFC 793 §3.4 figure 9)
approach:
[Objective]
Figure 9 in RFC 793: a stale (old duplicate) SYN reaches the LISTEN socket → SYN,ACK is sent → the real peer replies RST (because the SYN,ACK is unexpected) → DUT must accept the RST + return to LISTEN → fresh SYN works.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT in LISTEN.
2. Tester → DUT: stale SYN.
3. DUT → Tester: SYN,ACK.
4. Tester → DUT: RST with believable seq (= the SYN,ACK's ack_num).
5. Tester → DUT: fresh SYN.
6. Observation: DUT → Tester: SYN,ACK to the fresh SYN (LISTEN socket survived).

[Pass condition]
Both SYN,ACKs observed.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_first_syn_ack — DUT did not reply to the stale SYN
• Fail_no_second_syn_ack — DUT did not reply to the fresh SYN (LISTEN socket lost)

verdicts.Pass: DUT recovered from old duplicate SYN — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_first_syn_ack: No DUT SYN,ACK to first SYN
verdicts.Fail_no_second_syn_ack: No DUT SYN,ACK after old duplicate recovery
